title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
corePattern: Greedy Single Pass with Running Minimum - Prefix Minimum State Tracking
interviewTips: Clarify constraints: only one buy-sell transaction allowed, must buy before sell, return 0 if no profit possible, and ask about input size and empty array handling.

Trade-off discussion: Brute force O(n^2) is simple but fails for large n, DP state machine shows structured thinking, one-pass greedy achieves optimal O(n) time and O(1) space - explain why greedy is safe due to optimal substructure.

Edge-case tip: explicitly handle empty array, single element, strictly decreasing prices like [7,6,4,3,1] where answer is 0 not negative, and large values to avoid integer overflow in other languages.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force
approaches.intuition: Try every possible pair of buy day i and sell day j where j is after i, compute profit prices[j] - prices[i], and keep the maximum. This directly models the definition of best transaction.
approaches.theory: For all 0 <= i < j < n, evaluate profit. The answer is max over all pairs and 0 if all profits are negative. Double loop enumerates n*(n-1)/2 pairs, so correctness follows by exhaustive search. No extra state is needed.

timeComplexity.explanation: Two nested loops check all i<j pairs, about n*(n-1)/2 iterations, each O(1) work.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only a few integer variables for max profit and loop indices.

steps: i=0 price 7: best sell after is 6, profit -1, max stays 0
i=1 price 1: pairs give 4,2,5,3, max becomes 5 from buy 1 sell 6
i=2 price 5: best later is 6 profit 1, max stays 5
i=3 price 3: best later is 6 profit 3, max stays 5
i=4 price 6: later only 4 profit negative, max stays 5

edgeCases: Empty or single element array returns 0
Time limit exceeded for n up to 1e5 due to quadratic time

approaches.name: Approach 2: Dynamic Programming - State Machine and Kadane
approaches.intuition: Think of holding vs not holding stock. Each day you either keep previous decision or transition. Alternatively view price differences as array and find maximum subarray sum, which is Kadane logic.
approaches.theory: Define hold = max profit when holding one stock, cash = max profit when not holding. Initialize hold = -prices[0], cash = 0. Transition: hold = max(hold, -price), cash = max(cash, hold + price). This encodes at most one buy. Equivalent to Kadane on diff[i] = prices[i] - prices[i-1] with cur = max(0, cur + diff). By induction cash equals optimal profit for prefix.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single linear scan over prices with O(1) transition per element.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only two state variables hold and cash, DP array compressed from O(n) to O(1).

edgeCases: Empty array returns 0 without accessing prices[0]
Single element [5] returns 0, loop does not run
Large n up to 1e5 easily fits linear time

approaches.name: Approach 3: Optimal One-Pass Greedy with Minimum Price
approaches.intuition: Best sell day wants the lowest buy price before it. Scan left to right, remember minimum price seen so far, and profit if sold today. Keep global best.
approaches.theory: Maintain minPrice = min(prices[0..i]) and maxProfit = max(prices[i] - min prefix). For each i, any optimal transaction ending at or before i either uses current min or earlier best. Updating both in one pass yields optimal by prefix optimality. This is greedy because lowest prefix is always best buy for future sell.

timeComplexity.explanation: One linear pass, constant work per price to update min and best profit.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only minPrice and maxProfit variables regardless of input size.

edgeCases: Decreasing [5,4,3,2,1] min keeps dropping max stays 0
Increasing [1,2,3,4,5] profit 4 from first to last
